mission_09: Before choosing an imputation strategy, understanding the pattern and mechanism of missingness is crucial. Missing data can follow three mechanisms: MCAR (Missing Completely at Random) where missingness is unrelated to any values, MAR (Missing at Random) where missingness depends on observed variables, and MNAR (Missing Not at Random) where missingness depends on the unobserved values themselves. Analyzing missing patterns involves computing per-column missingness rates, identifying common combinations of missing columns, and examining correlations between missingness indicators. This analysis informs the choice of imputation method: simple methods suffice for MCAR, while MAR and MNAR require more sophisticated approaches like MICE or indicator variables. Proper pattern analysis prevents inappropriate imputation that could introduce bias or distort relationships in the data.
